key_insight: Finite-time wave collapse creates a nonunique post-blowup regime where vanishing regularization leads to spontaneous stochasticity and different limiting behaviors after collapse.
engineering_relevance: For dispersive wave systems, the result warns that post-collapse predictions may require probabilistic descriptions because viscous and saturating regularizations can agree before blowup yet diverge afterward.
method: Regularize a focusing Majda–McLaughlin–Tabak equation with either viscosity or nonlinear saturation.
Compare vanishing-regularization limits before and after finite-time collapse.
Use scale-by-scale fluctuation budgets to localize uncertainty production at collapse events.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical evidence that both regularizations recover the same inviscid collapse pre-blowup, but yield different post-blowup limits, with viscosity causing anomalous mass dissipation while saturation remains conservative.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a specific collapsing wave model and numerical vanishing-regularization studies, so generalization to other dispersive systems or experiments may need case-specific validation.
paper_title: Spontaneous stochasticity and anomalous dissipation in collapsing wave turbulence
